items.title: Motorcycle Oil Grades Explained
items.meta: Understanding SAE viscosity ratings, JASO MA/MA2, and API classifications.
items.searchText: motorcycle oil grades explained understanding sae viscosity ratings, jaso ma/ma2, and api classifications. sae viscosity the first number (e.g. 10 w-40) indicates cold-start viscosity. the w means winter. lower numbers flow better in cold conditions. the second number (e.g. 10w- 40 ) indicates viscosity at operating temperature. higher numbers provide thicker protection at high heat. jaso certification jaso ma — standard for wet-clutch motorcycles. no friction modifiers that cause clutch slip. jaso ma2 — higher friction performance for modern bikes. preferred for most current motorcycles. jaso mb — for scooters with cvt. not suitable for manual-clutch bikes. api rating look for api sg or higher. avoid automotive oils with energy-conserving labels — they contain friction modifiers harmful to wet clutches.

items.title: Contributing to MotoX Wiki
items.meta: How to add or update motorcycle specifications.
items.searchText: contributing to motox wiki how to add or update motorcycle specifications. how to contribute motox wiki is community-maintained. you can contribute by: forking the repository on github editing data/motorcycles.json , data/pages.json , or data/settings.json running npm run build:data to regenerate indexes and detail files committing changes and opening a pull request data guidelines always cite the source (service manual, oem documentation, manufacturer spec sheet) include year ranges and market/region when specs vary use standard units (nm for torque, l for volume, hp/kw for power) with conversions in parentheses put general specs in sections.general_specs and service figures in sections.service leave a field out rather than filling it with a generic value — an empty field is better than wrong data mark unverified data in the notes field or a custom section

items.meta: Typical dry torque values for common metric bolts and nuts by property class.
items.searchText: metric fastener torque guide typical dry torque values for common metric bolts and nuts by property class. typical dry torque values use these values only as a general reference for clean, dry, lightly oiled or plated threads where the manufacturer does not specify a torque. always prefer the torque figure in the official workshop manual, especially for engine, brake, suspension and safety-critical fasteners. thread 8.8 10.9 12.9 m5 5.5 nm 8 nm 9.5 nm m6 9.5 nm 14 nm 16.5 nm m8 23 nm 34 nm 40 nm m10 46 nm 68 nm 80 nm m12 80 nm 117 nm 140 nm m14 128 nm 187 nm 225 nm m16 197 nm 290 nm 345 nm notes these are approximate dry-thread values for metric coarse threads. lubricated threads can require 20–30% less torque for the same clamp load. reduce torque for aluminium threads, hollow fasteners, banjo bolts and fasteners into plastic. use a calibrated torque wrench and tighten in stages where a sequence is specified. never reuse torque-to-yield or single-use fasteners.
